hypotheses.text: In the index Sleyp et al. (2022) cohort of 14 individuals with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, global developmental delay/intellectual disability is fully penetrant (14/14, 100%), whereas seizures (including febrile seizures and unprovoked epilepsy) show incomplete penetrance, being present in fewer than 80% (<11/14) of patients.
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying the exact penetrance of seizures compared to neurodevelopmental delay in the defining clinical cohort determines whether absence of seizures can exclude KLHL20-related NEDSFBA in a young child with developmental delay.

evidence.text: Sleyp et al. evaluated 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, noting that intellectual disability was present across patients while the epilepsy phenotype was variable and limited, with at least 2 patients presenting solely with febrile seizures and 2 progressing from febrile seizures.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum …
source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features. We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]).

evidence.text: The detailed clinical description reports global developmental delay and seizures (Table 2), highlighting limited epilepsy phenotype with 2 having only febrile seizures and 2 having febrile seizures progressing to an unclear outcome.

hypotheses.text: Facial dysmorphisms reported across the 14 patients in Sleyp et al. (2022) do not coalesce into a recognizable, recurrent syndromic facial gestalt, with no individual dysmorphic HPO term reaching a penetrance greater than 70% in the cohort.
hypotheses.rationale: If facial dysmorphic features are subtle, varied, and non-obligate, clinicians cannot use craniofacial gestalt alone to differentiate KLHL20-related NEDSFBA from general syndromic autism spectrum disorders or developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.

evidence.text: Sleyp et al. explicitly describe the facial features in their 14 patients as subtle dysmorphic facial features rather than a distinctive or uniform facial gestalt.

hypotheses.text: Patients harboring the recurrent de novo p.Gly357Arg variant (11 of 14 patients) exhibit higher penetrance of behavioral abnormalities (autism spectrum disorder and hyperactivity) than of refractory afebrile epilepsy.
hypotheses.rationale: Establishing the predominant clinical presentation of the major recurrent variant (p.Gly357Arg) allows clinicians to recognize whether the core phenotype is primarily neurobehavioral with incidental/febrile seizures rather than a classic severe intractable epileptic encephalopathy.

evidence.text: Out of 14 patients studied by Sleyp et al., 11 shared the recurrent de novo missense variant p.Gly357Arg in the Kelch domain, and the overall cohort was characterized by intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, and hyperactivity with variable seizure phenotypes.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum …
source.quote: We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]). The recurrent missense and the 3 other missense variants all clustered in the Kelch-type β-propeller domain of the KLHL20 protein, which shapes the substrate binding surface.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient numerator and denominator counts for specific seizure sub-types (febrile seizures, generalized tonic-clonic, focal, absence) in Table 2 and the supplementary material of Sleyp et al. (2022)?
new_directions.rationale: Directly isolating the specific seizure sub-types in the 14 patients will delineate whether febrile seizures predominate over unprovoked afebrile epilepsy, providing key diagnostic clarity.

new_directions.question_text: Which specific facial dysmorphic HPO terms are detailed in the supplementary tables of Sleyp et al. (2022) and in what exact proportion of the 14 patients does each feature appear?
new_directions.rationale: A line-item breakdown of individual facial features (e.g., broad nasal bridge, thin upper lip, hypertelorism) is required to determine if any single dysmorphism reaches statistical significance for clinical phenotyping.
